SEPARATELY, AND CORRECTING THIS TABLE: the first pass claimed the sixteen items are stored raw. Solving for the weights of the deposit's SDO score returns +1 on all sixteen with a zero intercept, reproducing it for 370 of 370 complete rows, while flipping the eight items the .sav marks (R) reproduces only 32 of 370. They are stored PRE-RECODED. Corroborated by polarity, which points the same way: the across-block correlation is +0.201 rather than negative and the (R) item mean (2.52) sits level with the forward mean (2.45), neither of which a raw table would show. The same test run on sj, rwa and unjust returns PRE-RECODED for all three, so this was a family-wide error. See verify_lys_2020_rape_3_kpnts.R.

Two findings, one of which corrected this table. PAIRING: the Polish comes from Grzesiak-Feldman's cited adaptation (CEEOL id=108624), whose Zalacznik 1 lists twenty numbered items; each of the twelve English labels in the .sav is a direct translation of exactly one of them and vice versa, so the correspondence is forced by content across a 20-item pool rather than assumed from position. It also predicts structure that holds: the six items the appendix marks (R) land exactly on the odd codes rwa1, rwa3, rwa5, rwa7, rwa9, rwa11, an alternating design matching the cons block in the same battery. STORAGE: solving for the weights of the deposit's rwa_sum returns +1 on all twelve with a zero intercept and reproduces it for 342 of 342 complete rows, while flipping the six reverse-worded items reproduces only 22 of 342 -- so the items are stored ALREADY RECODED, correcting this table's original claim that they were raw. That also explains why keying polarity is not usable as a route here: all twelve intercorrelate positively (across-block r = +0.160), exactly as pre-recoding predicts. VERIFIED because the pairing distinguishes every item from every other. NOT established: the response anchors. The appendix publishes a 6-point scale while this study administered 5 (paper and data agree), so its labels do not describe this administration and option_text is blank.

The source states the mapping and the response data confirms it. STATED: the deposit's Codebook sheet keys Q1..Q12 to their statements, and data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' reshapes `Q1 Q2 ... Q12 -> Q` renaming the reshape index to `item`, so the live bare integer is the Q number rather than an opaque index. The Codebook and Survey 1 sheets are byte-identical on 11 of 12 statements, an internal cross-check; the 12th is readable only in Survey 1 because the Codebook's Q4 cell is a broken reference ('0x17'). CONFIRMED: the workbook's Survey 1 sheet publishes % Correct per item, and the observed proportion of resp == 1 reproduces all twelve values exactly, max absolute difference 0.000e+00. LIMIT of that second route taken alone -- four items share 0.990909 and two share 0.972727, so the percentages by themselves leave those groups interchangeable: 48 of the 479,001,600 possible orderings reproduce all twelve. VERIFIED rests on the stated mapping, which names every item individually; the percentages corroborate it and would have caught a wrong ordering outside those ties. Item sets match at 12 items, resp sets at 0/1. CORRECTION, and the %-correct route is what settles it: this table originally shipped correct_response = 1 on all twelve items, which reads on a true/false item as 'the answer is True' and is wrong for the four False-keyed ones (4, 5, 6, 9). The field is now blank. The DATA was never wrong -- resp encodes correctness rather than the answer, and the same route proves it item by item: for each False-keyed item the observed share of resp == 1 equals the published % Correct exactly, so item 9 (a False statement) shows 0.9909 where a literal-answer coding would show 0.0091. There is therefore no scoring key expressible against this resp axis, which is why correct_response is blank and the True/False key lives in the note instead.

The codebook states the mapping item by item and the response ranges corroborate it. STATED: Codebook_Baseline.xlsx rows 124-137 give one row per item carrying its own wording and its own response ladder, keyed by a cleandata_pre column reading Q102..Q115; data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r selects num_range("Pre", 102:115) and pivots with names_to = "item", a number-preserving rename with no positional step. CORROBORATED: each item's observed range sits inside its own declared ladder, and the ladder lengths differ across section 2 in a way that would expose a misalignment -- Pre114 tops out at exactly 4 against a 4-level ladder, while Pre112 and Pre115 reach 5 and 7 against 6- and 8-level ladders because two offered levels went unchosen. Had the four general-use items been permuted, an item would have shown a response above its ladder length; none does. LIMIT: within section 1 the ten SAS items all share one 6-point ladder, so range alone does not separate them from each other -- their individual assignment rests on the codebook naming each one, which it does. Item sets match at 14 items, resp sets match.

The deposit's variable dictionary names all 36 mathwrit_std35_* variables and the live code is that name with the wave prefix stripped; the dictionary's 36 codes and the live 36 are the same set exactly. Because the renaming happened upstream of this repo (data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external analysis directory), the correspondence was tested against the data rather than read off a script, using a prediction the dictionary makes and the responses can refute: a code the dictionary defines only with a b_ prefix must appear only at wave 0, and one defined only with e1_/e2_ must never appear at wave 0. Six codes are baseline-only (hvy_obj, sol_a..sol_e) and five endline-only (add3d_c, add3d_d, mul_d, mul_e, subt3d_d), so 11 of 36 are testable, and all 11 hold -- the six appear at wave 0 alone, the five at waves 0.5 and 1 only, and all 25 remaining codes span baseline and endline as predicted. PARTIAL for two reasons. First, the route does not separate the 25 all-wave codes from each other, nor members of a task family from each other; their assignment rests on the dictionary naming each variable. Second and more important, the shipped item_text is a task description rather than the literal problem, because the study used four parallel forms with differing numerals and the live table records no form -- so several items share identical item_text by necessity. Item sets match at 36, resp sets at 0/1.

What is verified here is the SUBSCALE STRUCTURE, not the wording, because no wording exists to verify. Solving M %*% w = y for the deposit's cult_cons and ec_cons scores over cons1..cons20 returns weights of exactly 1 on ten items and 0 on the other ten with a zero intercept, and reproduces both composites for all 385 complete rows to a maximum residual of 6.04e-14. The selection is the odd items for cult_cons and the even items for ec_cons, and the two sets partition all twenty with no overlap -- so the scale alternates subscales, which is what the two shipped sections record. Solved rather than read off correlations: a correlation ranking put cons14 apparently negative on ec_cons, which the exact solve shows to be nothing more than cross-loading noise. PARTIAL because item_text is blank for all twenty items (the .sav labels are bare 'conservatism itemN' strings and the paper reproduces two of twenty, unkeyed), option_text is blank (the paper states a 5-point scale but never its anchors), and nothing here distinguishes one item from another WITHIN a subscale. Item sets match at 20, resp sets at 1-5.
